lessons: Check `gov accept`'s outcome on every line, not only the totals. Keep suite output outside the worktree before any rebuild. Reproduce a red with the lead's exact pytest options.
proposed_decisions: P-W2-92-5, which blocks DONE and the merge. (1) Context: DEC-1006 P-1 (a) made the record-graph read soft; the supersession and must-not-cite filter (DEC-423, W2-55) reads from that same graph. (2) What happened: W1-21's case is red, alone too: with no record graph, superseded decisions are cited as current. At the base the read refused, which is the test's error branch. (3) Why it matters: a citation guard fails open in ordinary work (a half-loaded store); the old test enforces a standing decision. (4) Options: (a) keep P-1, but when the record graph cannot be read, cite no evidence from a record file, and say so in the closure facet. f3 and W1-21 both go green. About 15-25 lines in retrieve.py; it touches W2-55's area, so it is P2 and needs the CTO; one engineer batch plus the scoped run, about 1.5 h. (b) Revert P-1: refuse with STORE_MISSING as at the base, re-baseline KPI 3 to the code index only, and have a test designer retire f3. Same cost; no risk to the guard; KPI 3 loses its record-store half. (c) Weaken W1-21: rejected, because it fails open. (d) Rebuild the supersession map from front matter: rejected, because register-only supersessions would still be missed. (5) Recommendation: (a), confidence medium-high; (b) if W2-55's area must stay untouched this wave. Classification: ordinary work yes; consequence: fails open. (6) It blocks DONE, the merge, and W2-13's start on retrieve.py. It does not block anything else: all other work is done and verified.
